results.title: Chebyshev coefficients and Chebyshev truncation
results.informal: For $f$ continuous on $[-1,1]$, $a_k(f) = \tfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi f(\cos\theta)\cos(k\theta)\,d\theta$ for $k \ge 1$ (with $\tfrac{1}{\pi}$ for $k=0$) and the Chebyshev truncation is $f_n = \sum_{k \le n} a_k(f)\,T_k$. Characterised by the weighted inner product $\int f T_k (1-x^2)^{-1/2}$, exact on polynomials, and bounded by $2\max_{[-1,1]}|f|$.
results.conclusion: $a_k(f) = \tfrac{2}{\pi}\int_{-1}^{1} f(x)T_k(x)(1-x^2)^{-1/2}\,dx$ for $k \ge 1$ ($\tfrac{1}{\pi}$ for $k = 0$); $f \mapsto a_k(f)$ is linear; $a_k(T_m) = \delta_{km}$; if $\deg p \le n$ then $a_k(p) = 0$ for $k > n$ and $p_n = \sum_{k \le n} a_k(p)\,T_k = p$; $|a_0(f)| \le \max_{[-1,1]}|f|$ and $|a_k(f)| \le 2\max_{[-1,1]}|f|$

results.title: Bernstein ellipse
results.informal: For $\rho > 1$, $E_\rho = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z-1| + |z+1| < \rho + \rho^{-1}\}$, the open region bounded by the ellipse with foci $\pm 1$ and semi-axis sum $\rho$; equivalently the Joukowski image $\{(w + w^{-1})/2 : \rho^{-1} < |w| < \rho\}$. On $[a,b]$ one uses its affine image with foci $a, b$.
hypotheses: for the interval version: $a < b$ and $\varphi(t) = \tfrac{(b-a)t + (b+a)}{2}$
results.conclusion: $E_\rho$ is open, increasing in $\rho$ and contains $[-1,1]$; $E_\rho = J(\{\rho^{-1} < |w| < \rho\})$ with $J(w) = (w + w^{-1})/2$; every $z \in \overline{E_\rho}$ has $|z| \le \tfrac{\rho+\rho^{-1}}{2}$ and $\operatorname{Re} z \ge -\tfrac{\rho+\rho^{-1}}{2}$; $|T_n(z)| \le \tfrac{\rho^n + \rho^{-n}}{2}$ on $\overline{E_\rho}$; every $z \in \varphi(\overline{E_\rho})$ has $\operatorname{Re} z \ge \tfrac{(b+a) - (b-a)(\rho+\rho^{-1})/2}{2}$ and $|z| \le \tfrac{|b+a| + (b-a)(\rho+\rho^{-1})/2}{2}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: T_n(cos θ) = cos(nθ) for complex θ gives T_n(J(w)) = (w^n + w^{-n})/2

results.title: Best uniform approximation error E_n(f; [a,b])
results.informal: $E_n(f;[a,b]) = \inf\{E : \exists p,\ \deg p \le n,\ |f - p| \le E \text{ on } [a,b]\}$, written as an `sInf` in the `IsLeast` style of `isLeast_chebyshev_minimax`. For continuous $f$ the infimum is attained, decreases to $0$ (Weierstrass), and is invariant under affine change of variable.
results.conclusion: there is $p^*$ with $\deg p^* \le n$ and $\max_{[a,b]}|f - p^*| = E_n(f)$; $E_{n+1}(f) \le E_n(f) \le \max_{[a,b]}|f|$ and $E_n(f) \to 0$; $E_n(f + p) = E_n(f)$ for $\deg p \le n$, $E_n(cf) = |c|\,E_n(f)$, $E_n(f+g) \le E_n(f) + E_n(g)$; $E_n(f;[a,b]) = E_n(f\circ\varphi;[-1,1])$ for the affine bijection $\varphi : [-1,1] \to [a,b]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Weierstrass, ε-form: gives E_n(f) → 0

results.notes: Convention: theorems keep the existential form `∃ p, p.degree ≤ n ∧ ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, |f x - p.eval x| ≤ E` that NLAlib already uses; E_n is for statements whose sharp form needs the infimum (Lebesgue, equioscillation, de la Vallée Poussin) and for Lanczos-FA bounds stated with δ_k (Musco–Musco–Sidford 2018, T1). results.title: Lebesgue function and constant of polynomial interpolation
results.informal: For distinct nodes $x_0,\dots,x_n \in [a,b]$ with Lagrange basis $\ell_j$, $\lambda(x) = \sum_j |\ell_j(x)|$ and $\Lambda = \max_{[a,b]}\lambda$. $\Lambda$ is the operator norm of interpolation on $C[a,b]$, and interpolation is near-best: $\|f - p\| \le (1+\Lambda)E_n(f)$ (ATAP Thm 15.1).
hypotheses: $f$ continuous on $[a,b]$ and $p$ its interpolant (`Lagrange.interpolate`) at $v$
results.conclusion: $\Lambda \ge 1$; $|p(x)| \le \lambda(x)\max_j |f(v_j)|$, with equality for some $f$ with $\max|f| = 1$, so $\Lambda$ is the operator norm of interpolation; $\max_{[a,b]}|f - p| \le (1 + \Lambda)\,E_n(f;[a,b])$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Σ ℓ_j = 1 gives Λ ≥ 1
interpolation reproduces polynomials of degree ≤ n

results.title: Convergence of Chebyshev series (ATAP Thm 3.1)
aliases: uniform convergence of the Chebyshev expansion
results.informal: If $f$ is Lipschitz on $[-1,1]$ then $\sum_k |a_k| < \infty$ and $f = \sum_k a_k T_k$ absolutely and uniformly. The working half: whenever $f$ is continuous and $\sum |a_k| < \infty$, $\max_{[-1,1]}|f - f_n| \le \sum_{k>n}|a_k|$.
results.conclusion: under (a), $f(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} a_k T_k(x)$ for every $x \in [-1,1]$ and $\max_{[-1,1]}|f - f_n| \le \sum_{k > n}|a_k|$; (b) implies (a), and the Chebyshev series representation is unique

mathlib_prereqs.note: for g(θ) = f(cos θ) on AddCircle (2π), whose Fourier coefficients are a_|k|/2

results.notes: Prove (a) (difficulty 3): it is the bridge every rate theorem uses (7.2, 8.2, aliasing). results.title: Aliasing of Chebyshev polynomials and interpolant coefficients (ATAP Thms 4.1–4.2)
aliases: interpolation error at most twice the truncation tail
results.informal: On the Chebyshev grid $x_j = \cos(j\pi/n)$, $T_m$, $T_{2n\pm m}$, $T_{4n\pm m}, \dots$ take the same values; hence the interpolant $p_n$ has coefficients $c_k = a_k + \sum_{\ell \ge 1}(a_{2\ell n + k} + a_{2\ell n - k})$ and $\max|f - p_n| \le 2\sum_{k>n}|a_k|$.
hypotheses: $n \ge 1$, $0 \le m \le n$, grid $x_j = \cos(j\pi/n)$, $0 \le j \le n$ (Mathlib `Polynomial.Chebyshev.node n j`)
for the coefficient formula: $f$ continuous on $[-1,1]$ with $\sum_k |a_k| < \infty$, $p_n$ its interpolant in the grid with Chebyshev coefficients $c_k$
results.conclusion: $T_m(x_j) = T_{2\ell n + m}(x_j) = T_{2\ell n - m}(x_j)$ for all $\ell \ge 1$ and all $j$; $c_0 = a_0 + a_{2n} + a_{4n} + \cdots$, $c_n = a_n + a_{3n} + a_{5n} + \cdots$, and $c_k = a_k + \sum_{\ell \ge 1}(a_{2\ell n + k} + a_{2\ell n - k})$ for $1 \le k \le n-1$; consequently $\max_{[-1,1]}|f - p_n| \le 2\sum_{k > n}|a_k|$

mathlib_prereqs.note: cos(iπ/n): exactly ATAP's Chebyshev points
Chebyshev–Gauss quadrature at the zeros of T_n: the first-kind relative of the aliasing identity

results.notes: Thm 4.1 alone is difficulty 1 (T_k(cos(jπ/n)) = cos(kjπ/n)). ATAP states 4.2 for Lipschitz f; the summable hypothesis is what consumers have and avoids 3.1(b). First-kind variant at NLAlib's `chebyshevZero` (zeros of T_{n+1}): T_{2(n+1)-m} = -T_m there, and the same factor-2 bound holds. Consumers: the interpolant halves of chebyshev-approx-differentiable (4V) and chebyshev-approx-analytic (4M); Chebyshev-interpolation estimators of tr f(A). Prove.

results.title: Chebyshev coefficients of analytic functions (ATAP Thm 8.1)
results.informal: If $f$ extends analytically to the open Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho$ with $|f| \le M$ there, then $|a_0| \le M$ and $|a_k| \le 2M\rho^{-k}$ for $k \ge 1$.
hypotheses: $F : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ complex-differentiable on the open Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho$ with $|F(z)| \le M$ for $z \in E_\rho$
$F(x) = f(x)$ for $x \in [-1,1]$, and $a_k$ the Chebyshev coefficients of $f$
results.conclusion: $|a_0(f)| \le M$ and $|a_k(f)| \le 2M\rho^{-k}$ for all $k \ge 1$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Cauchy–Goursat on an annulus: moves the contour from |w| = 1 to |w| = r < ρ

results.notes: Proof: with J(w) = (w + w^{-1})/2, a_k = (1/(πi)) ∮_{|w|=1} F(J(w)) w^{-k-1} dw; F∘J is holomorphic on ρ^{-1} < |w| < ρ, so the integral equals the one over |w| = r for any 1 < r < ρ, which is at most 2M r^{-k}; let r ↑ ρ. Consumers: chebyshev-approx-analytic, hence bernstein-ellipse-approx, slq-error (general analytic f, ucs17 Thm 4.1), slit-plane-analytic-approx, lanczos-quadrature-analytic-error. Prove.

results.title: Convergence of Chebyshev approximations for analytic functions (ATAP Thm 8.2)
aliases: Chebyshev projection and interpolant error for analytic f
results.informal: Under Thm 8.1's hypotheses, $\|f - f_n\| \le \dfrac{2M\rho^{-n}}{\rho - 1}$ and $\|f - p_n\| \le \dfrac{4M\rho^{-n}}{\rho - 1}$ for every $n \ge 0$; the best-approximation corollary $E_n(f) \le \dfrac{2M\rho^{-n}}{\rho-1}$ is the existing candidate `bernstein-ellipse-approx`.
hypotheses: $F : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ complex-differentiable on the open Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho$ with $|F(z)| \le M$ for $z \in E_\rho$
$F(x) = f(x)$ for $x \in [-1,1]$, and $a_k$ the Chebyshev coefficients of $f$
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f_n$ the Chebyshev truncation and $p_n$ the interpolant in the $(n+1)$-point Chebyshev grid
results.conclusion: $\max_{[-1,1]}|f - f_n| \le \dfrac{2M\rho^{-n}}{\rho - 1}$ and $\max_{[-1,1]}|f - p_n| \le \dfrac{4M\rho^{-n}}{\rho - 1}$; transplanted to $[a,b]$: if $f \circ \varphi$ satisfies the hypotheses then some $p$ with $\deg p \le n$ has $|f(x) - p(x)| \le \tfrac{2M\rho^{-n}}{\rho - 1}$ for $x \in [a,b]$
results.notes: The truncation half needs only 8.1 and 3.1(a) (sum a geometric tail); the interpolant half needs aliasing. Suggest adding the edge bernstein-ellipse-approx → chebyshev-approx-analytic in atlas.json (the existing candidate is this theorem's E_n corollary). Consumers: bernstein-ellipse-approx, slq-error (general analytic f), lanczos-quadrature-analytic-error, slit-plane-analytic-approx, T1's Krylov f(A)b bound (Saad 1992 Thm 3.3 composed with this). Prove.

results.title: Chebyshev equioscillation theorem (ATAP Thm 10.1)
results.informal: A continuous real $f$ on $[a,b]$ has a unique best approximation $p^* \in \mathcal{P}_n$, and $p$ with $\deg p \le n$ is $p^*$ iff $f - p$ equioscillates at $n+2$ points: $a \le x_0 < \cdots < x_{n+1} \le b$ with $f(x_i) - p(x_i) = \sigma(-1)^i\max_{[a,b]}|f - p|$.
results.conclusion: $\max_{[a,b]}|f - p| = E_n(f;[a,b])$ if and only if there are $a \le x_0 < \cdots < x_{n+1} \le b$ and $\sigma \in \{\pm 1\}$ with $f(x_i) - p(x_i) = \sigma(-1)^i\max_{[a,b]}|f - p|$ for all $i$; the best approximation is unique

mathlib_prereqs.note: the extremal points of T_n: the model alternation set
no alternation theorem

results.notes: The 'if' direction is de-la-vallee-poussin with equal values; the 'only if' direction (perturbation argument) and uniqueness are the work. Consumers: optimality statements (chebyshev-monic-minimal and chebyshev-minimax are instances), Remez, sharp lower bounds for sign/exp. Assume if a consumer needs it; de la Vallée Poussin covers the lower-bound use.

results.title: De la Vallée Poussin lower bound for best approximation
results.informal: If $f - p$ ($\deg p \le n$) takes nonzero values of alternating sign at $n+2$ points of $[a,b]$, every polynomial of degree $\le n$ has error at least $\min_i |f(x_i) - p(x_i)|$ at one of those points, so $E_n(f) \ge \min_i|f(x_i) - p(x_i)|$.
hypotheses: $p \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg p \le n$ and $(f(x_i) - p(x_i))(f(x_{i+1}) - p(x_{i+1})) < 0$ for $0 \le i \le n$
results.conclusion: for every $q \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg q \le n$, $\max_{0 \le i \le n+1}|f(x_i) - q(x_i)| \ge \min_{0 \le i \le n+1}|f(x_i) - p(x_i)|$; hence $E_n(f;[a,b]) \ge \min_i|f(x_i) - p(x_i)|$
results.notes: Proof: if q beat the minimum at every x_i, q - p would have the sign of f - p at the n+2 points, hence n+1 roots, hence q = p: contradiction. The discrete form needs no continuity of f. Consumers: equioscillation; explicit lower-bound certificates for approximating sign, exp and 1/x; generalises the lower half of chebyshev-minimax. Prove.

results.title: Lebesgue constant of Chebyshev interpolation (ATAP Thm 15.2)
results.informal: For interpolation in the $n+1$ Chebyshev points $\cos(j\pi/n)$, $\Lambda_n \le \tfrac{2}{\pi}\log(n+1) + 1$; with Thm 15.1, $\|f - p_n\| \le (2 + \tfrac{2}{\pi}\log(n+1))E_n(f)$.
results.conclusion: $\Lambda_n = \max_{x \in [-1,1]}\sum_{j=0}^{n}|\ell_j(x)| \le \tfrac{2}{\pi}\log(n+1) + 1$; hence $\max_{[-1,1]}|f - p_n| \le \big(2 + \tfrac{2}{\pi}\log(n+1)\big)E_n(f)$ for continuous $f$
results.notes: The first-kind analogue (zeros of T_{n+1}, NLAlib `chebyshevZero`) has a bound of the same form (Rivlin); pin the printed label before stating it. Consumers: near-best Chebyshev interpolation (turns jackson-lipschitz / chebyshev-approx-analytic E_n bounds into interpolant bounds with a log factor), KPM practice. Assume; low priority for RandNLA.

results.title: Jackson's theorem for Lipschitz functions
aliases: degree of approximation of Lipschitz functions
results.informal: If $f$ is $\lambda$-Lipschitz on $[-1,1]$ then $E_n(f) \le \dfrac{\pi\lambda}{2(n+1)}$; on $[a,b]$, $E_n(f) \le \dfrac{\pi\lambda(b-a)}{4(n+1)}$.
results.conclusion: $\exists p$ with $\deg p \le n$ and $|f(x) - p(x)| \le \dfrac{\pi\lambda(b-a)}{4(n+1)}$ for all $x \in [a,b]$ (on $[-1,1]$: $\tfrac{\pi\lambda}{2(n+1)}$)

results.title: Bernstein's growth lemma on the Bernstein ellipse
results.informal: If $\deg p \le n$ and $|p| \le M$ on $[-1,1]$ then $|p(z)| \le M\rho^n$ on the closed Bernstein ellipse $\overline{E_\rho}$: the complex counterpart of `chebyshev-extremal`.
hypotheses: $p \in \mathbb{C}[x]$ with $\deg p \le n$ and $|p(x)| \le M$ for $x \in [-1,1]$
results.conclusion: $|p(z)| \le M\rho^n$ for every $z \in \overline{E_\rho}$; equivalently $|p(J(w))| \le M|w|^n$ for $|w| \ge 1$, $J(w) = (w + w^{-1})/2$

results.title: Lanczos (Gauss) quadrature error for analytic f
aliases: quadratic form b^T f(A) b by Lanczos
results.informal: If $A$ is symmetric with spectrum in $[a,c]$ and $f\circ\varphi$ extends analytically to $E_\rho$ with $|\cdot| \le M$, then $q$ Lanczos steps give $\big|b^\top f(A)b - (Q^\top b)^\top f(Q^\top A Q)\,Q^\top b\big| \le \dfrac{4M\rho^{1-2q}}{\rho - 1}\|b\|^2$.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ symmetric with all eigenvalues in $[a,c]$, $a < c$, and $\varphi(t) = \tfrac{(c-a)t + (c+a)}{2}$
$\rho > 1$; $F$ complex-differentiable on $E_\rho$ with $|F| \le M$ there and $F(t) = f(\varphi(t))$ for $t \in [-1,1]$
results.conclusion: $\big|b^\top f(A)b - (Q^\top b)^\top f(Q^\top A Q)(Q^\top b)\big| \le \dfrac{4M\rho^{1-2q}}{\rho - 1}\,b^\top b$
results.notes: One line once chebyshev-approx-analytic exists: NLAlib `abs_dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_le_of_krylovSpace_le` with p the transplanted Chebyshev truncation of degree 2q-1 and E = 2Mρ^{1-2q}/(ρ-1). Consumers: slq-error for general analytic f (log-determinant, tr exp(-tA), tr A^{-1/2}); suggest adding the edge slq-error → lanczos-quadrature-analytic-error. ATAP Ch. 19's (64/15)Mρ^{-2q}/(ρ²-1) is for the Legendre weight and is not directly comparable. Prove.

results.title: Lanczos (Gauss) quadrature error for Lipschitz f (Wasserstein form)
results.informal: For $L$-Lipschitz $f$ on $[a,c]$, $\big|b^\top f(A)b - (Q^\top b)^\top f(Q^\top AQ)\,Q^\top b\big| \le \dfrac{\pi L(c-a)}{4q}\|b\|^2$; for unit $b$ this says $W_1(\mu_b, \hat\mu_q) \le \tfrac{\pi(c-a)}{4q}$ between the spectral measure and its $q$-point Gauss rule.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ symmetric with all eigenvalues in $[a,c]$, $a < c$, and $\varphi(t) = \tfrac{(c-a)t + (c+a)}{2}$
results.conclusion: $\big|b^\top f(A)b - (Q^\top b)^\top f(Q^\top A Q)(Q^\top b)\big| \le \dfrac{\pi L(c-a)}{4q}\,b^\top b$

mathlib_prereqs.note: no Wasserstein distance or Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality; stated with test functions

results.notes: Derivation: Jackson with n = 2q-1 on [a,c] gives E ≤ πL(c-a)/(8q); the NLAlib Lanczos lemma doubles it. Consumers: spectral density estimation by SLQ (ctu21) and by moment matching (bkm22), eigenvalue counts with Lipschitz-smoothed indicators. Prove once jackson-lipschitz is assumed.

results.title: Low-degree approximation of x^s (Sachdeva–Vishnoi Thm 3.3)
results.informal: $x^s = \sum_{j=0}^{s} 2^{-s}\binom{s}{j}T_{|s-2j|}(x)$; keeping the terms with $|s - 2j| \le d$ gives $p_{s,d}$ of degree $\le d$ with $\max_{[-1,1]}|x^s - p_{s,d}| \le 2e^{-d^2/(2s)}$, so degree $\sqrt{2s\log(2/\varepsilon)}$ suffices for error $\varepsilon$.
results.conclusion: $x^s = \sum_{j=0}^{s} 2^{-s}\binom{s}{j}\,T_{|s-2j|}(x)$ as polynomials, and $p_{s,d} = \sum_{j\,:\,|s-2j| \le d} 2^{-s}\binom{s}{j}\,T_{|s-2j|}$ has $\deg p_{s,d} \le d$ and $|x^s - p_{s,d}(x)| \le 2e^{-d^2/(2s)}$ for $x \in [-1,1]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: 2 T_m T_k = T_{m+k} + T_{m-k}; with m = 1 gives x T_k = (T_{k+1} + T_{k-1})/2
Chernoff bound for the binomial tail

results.notes: The binomial tail Σ_{|s-2j|>d} 2^{-s} C(s,j) ≤ 2e^{-d²/(2s)} is proved from Σ_j C(s,j) e^{λ(s-2j)} = (2 cosh λ)^s and `Real.cosh_le_exp_half_sq`, without probability (Polynomial is layer 0 and cannot import Concentration). Consumers: exp-polynomial-approx; the 'Lanczos with q steps matches power iteration with q² steps' comparison behind random-start-power (kw92) and block Krylov vs subspace iteration (mm15); polynomial approximation of matrix powers. Prove.

results.title: Polynomial approximation of e^{-x} on [0,b] (Sachdeva–Vishnoi Thm 4.1)
results.informal: For $b > 0$ and $0 < \delta \le 1$, with $t = \lceil\max(e^2 b/2, \log(2/\delta))\rceil$ and $d = \lceil\sqrt{2t\log(4/\delta)}\rceil$, some $p$ of degree $\le d$ has $|e^{-x} - p(x)| \le \delta$ on $[0,b]$: degree $O\big(\sqrt{\max(b, \log(1/\delta))\log(1/\delta)}\big)$ with the constants shown. For $e^{-\tau x}$ on $[0,\beta]$ take $b = \tau\beta$.
results.conclusion: $\exists p \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg p \le d$ and $|e^{-x} - p(x)| \le \delta$ for all $x \in [0,b]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Taylor remainder only for |x| ≤ 1; the Poisson tail Σ_{i≥t}(b/2)^i/i! ≤ e^{b/2}(eb/(2t))^t must be proved

results.notes: Constants derived here following the SV proof (SV state the degree with O(·)): write e^{-x} = e^{-b/2}e^{-(b/2)y}, y = 2x/b - 1; truncate the Taylor series at t terms (tail ≤ (eb/(2t))^t ≤ e^{-t} ≤ δ/2); replace each y^i, 1 ≤ i < t, by p_{i,d} at total cost ≤ 2e^{-d²/(2t)} ≤ δ/2. Consumers: tr exp(-τA) (heat-kernel trace, Estrada index) by SLQ / Hutch++, exp(-τA)b by Lanczos (Musco–Musco–Sidford 2018), matrix multiplicative weights; optimality in exp-approx-lower-bound. Prove.

results.title: Degree lower bound for approximating e^{-x} on [0,b]
results.informal: If $\deg p \le q$ and $|p - e^{-x}| \le \delta \le 1/8$ on $[0,b]$ with $b \ge 1$, then $q^2 \ge \dfrac{(1 - e^{-1} - 2\delta)\,b}{2(1+\delta)}$; in particular $q \ge \sqrt{b/6}$.
hypotheses: $p \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg p \le q$ and $|p(x) - e^{-x}| \le \delta$ for $x \in [0,b]$
results.conclusion: $q^2 \ge \dfrac{(1 - e^{-1} - 2\delta)\,b}{2(1 + \delta)}$, hence $q \ge \sqrt{b/6}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: mean value theorem on [0,1]

results.notes: Constants derived here: the MVT on [0,1] gives |p'(ξ)| ≥ 1 - e^{-1} - 2δ; Markov on [0,b] (NLAlib `abs_eval_derivative_le_two_mul_sq_div_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le`) gives |p'(ξ)| ≤ 2q²(1+δ)/b. Shows the √b in exp-polynomial-approx is optimal. Consumers: optimality claims for Lanczos/Chebyshev exp(A)b and heat-trace estimation. Prove.

results.title: Approximation on [a,b] of functions analytic in the right half-plane (x^{-1/2}, log x, x^alpha)
results.informal: For $0 < a < b$, $\rho_0 = \tfrac{\sqrt b + \sqrt a}{\sqrt b - \sqrt a}$ and $1 < r < \rho_0$, the transplanted ellipse $\varphi(E_r)$ lies in $\{\operatorname{Re} z \ge m_r\}$ with $m_r = \tfrac{(b+a) - (b-a)(r + r^{-1})/2}{2} > 0$. So any $F$ analytic on $\operatorname{Re} z > 0$ with $|F| \le M$ there is approximated on $[a,b]$ to within $\tfrac{2Mr^{-n}}{r-1}$ by degree $n$; $M = \max(m_r^\alpha, R_r^\alpha)$ for $x^\alpha$ and $\max(|\log m_r|, |\log R_r|) + \pi/2$ for $\log x$.
hypotheses: $0 < a < b$, $\rho_0 = \tfrac{\sqrt b + \sqrt a}{\sqrt b - \sqrt a}$, $1 < r < \rho_0$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$
$F$ complex-differentiable on $\{\operatorname{Re} z > 0\}$, real on $[a,b]$, with $|F(z)| \le M$ whenever $\operatorname{Re} z \ge m_r$ and $|z| \le R_r$
results.conclusion: $m_r > 0$ and $\exists p$ with $\deg p \le n$ and $|F(x) - p(x)| \le \dfrac{2Mr^{-n}}{r - 1}$ for $x \in [a,b]$; for $F(z) = z^{\alpha}$ ($\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$) one may take $M = \max(m_r^{\alpha}, R_r^{\alpha})$, for $F = \operatorname{Log}$, $M = \max(|\log m_r|, |\log R_r|) + \pi/2$

mathlib_prereqs.note: NLAlib, not Mathlib: (b+a)/(b-a) + √(((b+a)/(b-a))² - 1) = (√b+√a)/(√b-√a), the same ρ₀

results.notes: r ↑ ρ₀ trades constant for rate; degree O(√κ log(κ/ε)) for x^{-1/2} and log. For 1/x it is weaker than NLAlib's inverse-polynomial-approx (variant). Consumers: slq-error with f = log (log-determinant, ucs17) and f = x^{-1/2}; Krylov methods for A^{-1/2}b (Gaussian sampling, whitening); sign-polynomial-approx; T1's Krylov f(A)b bounds for Stieltjes-type f. Prove.

results.title: Polynomial approximation of sign(x) away from 0
results.informal: For $0 < \gamma < 1$ and $1 < r < \tfrac{1+\gamma}{1-\gamma}$ there is an odd $p(x) = x\,q(x^2)$ of degree $\le 2n+1$ with $|\operatorname{sgn} x - p(x)| \le \tfrac{2m_r^{-1/2}r^{-n}}{r-1}$ for $\gamma \le |x| \le 1$ (the $x^{-1/2}$ bound on $[\gamma^2, 1]$). With $r = 1 + \gamma$ the bound is $\tfrac{4}{\sqrt3\,\gamma^2}(1+\gamma)^{-n}$: degree $O(\gamma^{-1}\log(1/(\gamma\varepsilon)))$. The step $\mathbf{1}[x \ge c]$ is $(1 + \operatorname{sgn}(x - c))/2$.
results.conclusion: $\exists q$ with $\deg q \le n$ such that $p(x) = x\,q(x^2)$ satisfies $|\operatorname{sgn}(x) - p(x)| \le \dfrac{2\,m_r^{-1/2}\,r^{-n}}{r - 1}$ for $\gamma \le |x| \le 1$; for $r = 1+\gamma$, $m_r = \gamma^2(3+\gamma)/4$ and the bound is at most $\dfrac{4}{\sqrt3\,\gamma^2}(1+\gamma)^{-n}$
results.notes: As r ↑ (1+γ)/(1-γ) the base per degree-2 step tends to (1-γ)/(1+γ), the exponential base of Eremenko–Yuditskii's sharp asymptotics (EY07 Thm 1; pin its exact constant before adding it as an assumed variant). A variant with |p| ≤ 1 on all of [-1,1] (needed for stable projector polynomials; Gilyén–Su–Low–Wiebe 2019) is later. Consumers: spectral projectors and principal component projection/regression (fmms16), eigenvalue counting in an interval (spectral density), gap-dependent block Krylov. Lower bound: sign-approx-lower-bound. Prove.

results.title: Degree lower bound for approximating sign(x) with a gap
results.informal: If $\deg p \le q$, $|p| \le M$ on $[-1,1]$ and $|p - \operatorname{sgn}| \le \varepsilon < 1$ on $\gamma \le |x| \le 1$, then $qM \ge \dfrac{(1-\varepsilon)\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}}{\gamma}$.
hypotheses: $p \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg p \le q$ and $|p(x)| \le M$ for $x \in [-1,1]$
results.conclusion: $q\,M \ge \dfrac{(1 - \varepsilon)\sqrt{1 - \gamma^2}}{\gamma}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: mean value theorem on [-γ, γ]

results.notes: Derivation: the MVT on [-γ,γ] gives ξ with p'(ξ) ≥ (1-ε)/γ; Bernstein (NLAlib `abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le`) gives |p'(ξ)| ≤ qM/√(1-γ²). Shows the 1/γ order in sign-polynomial-approx is optimal. Consumers: optimality of gap-dependent Krylov and projector rates. Prove.

results.title: Lower bound for polynomial approximation of 1/x on [a,b]
results.informal: If $\deg p < q$ and $|p(x) - 1/x| \le \varepsilon$ on $[a,b]$, then $\varepsilon \ge \tfrac{1}{b}\big(\tfrac{\sqrt b - \sqrt a}{\sqrt b + \sqrt a}\big)^q$; `inverse-polynomial-approx` is sharp up to the factor $2b/a$.
results.conclusion: $\varepsilon \ge \dfrac{1}{b\,T_q\big(\tfrac{b+a}{b-a}\big)} \ge \dfrac{1}{b}\Big(\dfrac{\sqrt b - \sqrt a}{\sqrt b + \sqrt a}\Big)^{q}$
results.notes: Proof: r = 1 - x p has degree ≤ q, r(0) = 1 and |r| ≤ bε on [a,b]; apply NLAlib `inv_eval_T_real_le_of_forall_abs_eval_le`, then `eval_T_real_le_pow` with `add_div_sub_add_sqrt_sq_sub_one_eq`. Consumers: optimality of the √κ rates of CG, Chebyshev iteration and Lanczos solves; lower bounds on iteration counts in sketch-and-precondition. Prove.
